client_question: Should we add pharmacy counters to our grocery stores?
acceptable_recommendations: Add pharmacy counters, starting with a pilot
key_risks: A national pharmacy chain near most of our stores keeps customers, so prescriptions fall short; hiring licensed pharmacists
next_steps: Pilot counters in 10 stores and track prescriptions filled per week before rolling out
model_answer: Add pharmacy counters, starting with a pilot. Each counter costs $400k and earns about $150k a year, paying back in under 3 years against our 4-year hurdle, and 60% of our shoppers fill prescriptions elsewhere every month. The main risk is that the national pharmacy chain near 80% of our stores keeps those customers, so the next step is a 10-store pilot that tracks prescriptions filled each week before we roll out.
